title: Work of Bus Safety Tripartite Taskforce and Stakeholder Engagement Efforts to Enhance Bus and Commuter Safety
what_it_is: Work of Bus Safety Tripartite Taskforce and Stakeholder Engagement Efforts to Enhance Bus and Commuter Safety

sections.label: Bus safety review engagement
sections.summary: The review builds on existing safety practices and engaged stakeholders between July and October 2024 to gather feedback on improving bus safety.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The review builds on the safety initiatives and practices that the Land Transport Authority, the public transport operators and workers have put in place over the years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: It aims to identify ways to make further improvements in areas such as safety protocols and procedures, staffing levels and work conditions, design of road infrastructure and the usage of technology.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Between July 2024 and October 2024, the Taskforce engaged stakeholders such as commuters, road users, bus captains and other public transport workers, to obtain their feedback on how to improve bus safety.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: This includes a one-month long public survey which gathered over 2,300 responses, a survey for our bus captains which garnered over 3,400 responses, as well as in-person focus group discussions with around 160 commuters and road users.

sections.label: Taskforce future engagement plans
sections.summary: The Taskforce will engage international experts, overseas regulators and operators, and aims to complete its review by the first half of 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: In the coming months, the Taskforce will be engaging international experts, overseas regulators and operators to identify suitable best practices that the local public bus sector can adopt.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The Taskforce aims to complete its review by the first half of 2025.

sections.label: Preliminary findings on bus safety
sections.summary: Surveys and engagements so far showed that commuters generally feel safety standards onboard buses are good.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: As to the preliminary findings, the surveys and engagements that the Taskforce had so far showed that commuters generally feel that the safety standards onboard buses are good.

sections.label: Concerns for seniors on buses
sections.summary: Areas of concern are dealing with quick deceleration and dissuading seniors with mobility issues from going to the upper deck.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In particular, one area of concern is how they would be dealing with situations where the bus had to decelerate quickly as that may cause problems for our seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The other area is also, sometimes, to dissuade seniors who have mobility issues from going to the upper deck in double-deck buses, but instead, to remain in the lower deck of the buses so that they do not take any chances while climbing up to the upper deck.
